What We Know About the Lab Worker Whose Death Has Triggered Mass Quarantine In Siberia Russian lab technician Darya Shipilova, 28, died after severe pneumonia, days after reportedly handling live plague bacteria at an anti-plague institute in Siberia. Rospotrebnadzor attributed her death to pneumonia of unknown aetiology, while Buryatia’s governor said it was plague. Nearly 200 contacts are reportedly under observation as authorities investigate safety violations at the institute. Tasneem Kanchwala Updated: Monday, October 05, 2026, 11:31 AM IST Who Is Darya Shipilova? What We Know About the Lab Worker Whose Death Has Triggered Mass Quarantine In Siberia | X/ @visegrad24 Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, Siberia, died overnight between October 1 and October 2 in the ICU of the Shelekhov district hospital, days after being hospitalised with severe pneumonia. Russian federal health body Rospotrebnadzor has officially attributed her death to "pneumonia of unknown aetiology," while the governor of the neighbouring Buryatia Republic has publicly stated she died of plague. One working theory is that she may have broken a test tube containing live plague bacteria while handling it at the institute around late September. Who is Darya Shipilova? According to a thread posted on X by the account International Cyber Digest, Shipilova joined the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute as a junior staff member in September 2022 at age 24, was earning approximately $850 a month, and was still formally listed as a student as recently as 2024. These specific details, her employment history, salary, and student status, have not been independently corroborated by mainstream outlets covering the story and should be treated as claims from that account's reporting rather than confirmed fact at this stage.
